newsitem.title: DENMARK: Carlsberg-Tetley H1 profits down 28 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Carlsberg-Tetley H1 profits down 28 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Carlsberg-Tetley, the British-based brewer owned jointly by Denmark's Carlsberg and Britain's Bass, logged first-half 1997 profit of 18 million pounds ($29.6 million), down from 28 million pounds in the same period of 1996, Carlsberg-Tetley said on Thursday.
Managing director Ebbe Dinsen told Reuters that, viewed as a whole, the accounts were actually stronger than in the first six months of last year, but one-off items hit the bottom line.
He declined to give further details, saying that further information would be given in Carlsberg's first-half report, to be published in the week commencing June 2.
Bass is seeking to buy Carlsberg's 50 percent of the partnership, seen as important in boosting its British business.
The planned deal, which would create Britain's largest brewer and give it 35 percent market share, is subject to approval by British authorities.
"We expect a decision within the next 14 days," Dinsen said.
